title: Python and research engineering
description: Turn a small calculation into a readable, testable, reproducible data artifact. Begin here if you have never run a research script.

title: Mathematics for ML
description: Use shapes, geometry, probability, and gradients to reason about a model before training it.

title: Classical ML and evaluation
description: Fit interpretable baselines and separate model selection, probability quality, and final assessment.

title: Deep learning foundations
description: Understand gradients and optimizer state, then diagnose a tiny training problem before scaling.

title: Transformers and language models
description: Follow text from tokens through masked objectives and parameter-efficient adaptation; evaluate the task rather than a fluent impression.

title: Representation learning and world models
description: Compare reconstruction, contrastive signals, latent prediction, and multi-step dynamics with explicit collapse checks.

title: Scientific ML and neural operators
description: Specify a PDE problem and boundary conditions, then compare operator and physics-informed approaches under rollout and resolution shift.

title: Memory, retrieval, and agents
description: Evaluate evidence retrieval separately from answer generation, then test memory interventions and bounded tool behavior.

title: Efficient ML systems
description: Measure numerical error, cache size, and queueing costs while keeping quality and latency comparisons fair.

title: ML for astronomy, weather, and materials
description: Keep provenance, availability time, scientific validation, and inverse-problem uncertainty explicit across domain applications.

title: Reinforcement learning and decision systems
description: Define transitions and returns, compute tiny value problems, then examine exploration and offline evidence limits.

title: Research practice
description: Convert a paper or idea into a falsifiable, resource-matched comparison with retained negative results and a reproducible report.
